title: Iranian cross-and-eight-point star study
application: Wall tile field or bounded feature panel
description: An original editable study of the cross-and-eight-point-star tessellation documented on thirteenth-century Iranian tiles in the V&A collection. It is not a tracing or fabrication drawing.
historicalContext: Iran · tile panel dated 1262 · V&A museum references listed in source
reviewPoints: Study the cited museum object before adapting the geometry
Commission an artist or specialist to resolve proportions and cultural context
Prototype joints, borders and cut tiles at full scale

title: Mughal hexagonal jali study
description: A hexagonal lattice study informed by the Met’s documentation of a seventeenth-century Mughal white-marble jali. The screen shown here is newly generated CSS geometry.
historicalContext: Mughal tradition · seventeenth century · white-marble jali documented by the Met
reviewPoints: Review the museum reference and regional context
Engineer support, opening sizes and edge safety
Model daylight, ventilation, privacy and cleaning

title: Mamluk star woodwork study
application: Door, minbar-adjacent joinery or wall panel study
description: A star-field concept informed by fourteenth-century Mamluk Egyptian doors described by the Met. It must not be represented as a replica or historic reconstruction.
historicalContext: Mamluk Egypt · fourteenth-century doors · complex star pattern and inlay
reviewPoints: Keep sacred and liturgical elements under qualified religious review
Engage a skilled craftsperson for joinery and material selection
Confirm fire, accessibility and maintenance requirements

source.label: Met Museum — The Nature of Islamic Ornament: Geometric Patterns
source.rights: Original CSS interpretation; referenced doors are not reproduced

title: Interlaced-circle construction study
description: A construction study using circles, one of the repeat-unit families identified by the Met’s Department of Islamic Art.
historicalContext: General Islamic geometric vocabulary · circles and interlaced circles
reviewPoints: Use as a geometry exercise rather than a claim of regional authenticity
Document the chosen proportion and construction method
Have final architectural use reviewed in its local cultural context

title: Square-and-polygon construction study
application: Paving, ceiling or panel module exploration
description: An editable square-and-polygon study based on the Met’s documented geometric vocabulary, not on a single copied monument.
historicalContext: General Islamic geometric vocabulary · squares and four-sided polygons
reviewPoints: Select a regional and material reference before design development
Coordinate module boundaries with movement joints and thresholds
Test contrast, slip and cleaning performance for the application

title: Radial polygon study

title: Nishapur kite-and-dart study

historicalContext: Nishapur, Iran · late thirteenth–fourteenth century tile context

title: Saff-alignment carpet module
description: A mosque.build planning diagram for comparing row spacing, seams, columns and accessible positions. This is functional prayer-space planning, not a historical ornament claim.

reviewPoints: Confirm qibla basis with accountable local review

title: Muqarnas transition diagram
description: A deliberately simplified diagram introducing muqarnas as clustered niche geometry. It is not structural geometry, shop drawing or permission to imitate a monument.
historicalContext: Islamic architectural vocabulary · muqarnas documented in the Met educator resource
reviewPoints: Appoint an architect and specialist craft designer
Separate structural support from decorative geometry
Review regional precedent, religious setting, fire and maintenance
